newsitem.title: UK: Tarmac says Comet wins Copenhagen metro bid.
newsitem.headline: Tarmac says Comet wins Copenhagen metro bid.

text.p: UK construction group Tarmac Plc said on Wednesday that the Copenhagen Metro Construction Group (Comet), of which it is a part, has been chosen as the preferred contractor for the design and construction of the city's first underground metro system.
Orestadsselskabet, which is responsible for implementing the metro system, has chosen Comet for all the civil works associated with the project, Tarmac said in a statement.
The Comet consortium comprises Tarmac Construction International, SAE International, Astaldi SpA, Bachy Ltd, Ilbau GmbH and Christiani & Nielsen A/S.

"Final discussions are now underway with Comet with the aim of concluding a formal contract by the end of September. The final value of the contract is still to be determined but is anticipated to be in the region of 300-400 million stg," Tarmac said.

"We are delighted to have been chosen as the preferred contractor for this major development. All of the Comet companies have considerable experience of major civil engineering work throughout the world and each will bring their own individual skills to the project," said Brian Pollard, Tarmac Construction's chief executive.

Tarmac said Comet's work would involve "extensive tunnelling under the city of Copenhagen together with viaducts and embankments for the section of the Metro on the island of Amerger where a new township is to be developed".
The contract also includes the construction of 14 stations, of which six will be deep underground stations.
